gps.help_intro: To include GPS coordinates in photo certification, location permission must be allowed in both your browser and operating system. Check the guide that matches your environment.
gps.help_ios_safari_body:
① Reset site permission (most reliable): Settings → Safari → Advanced → Website Data → search 'ori.pics' → swipe left → Delete → revisit site and tap Allow on the permission prompt
② Safari location policy: Settings → Safari → Location → Ask or Allow
③ iOS Location Services: Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services On → Safari Websites → While Using the App + Precise Location On
gps.help_ios_chrome_body:
iOS Chrome manages permissions separately from Safari. Unlike Android Chrome, iOS Chrome does NOT have a per-site Content Settings → Location menu. Try the following in order.
① iOS system location permission (required): Settings app → Privacy & Security → Location Services On → on the same screen, find 'Chrome' → While Using the App + Precise Location On
② Reset per-site permission: Chrome bottom-right ⋯ menu → Settings → Privacy → Clear Browsing Data → Time Range: All time → check 'Cookies, Site Data' → Clear Browsing Data → revisit ori.pics, and tap Allow on the permission prompt
③ Force-quit Chrome and relaunch: open the App Switcher (swipe up from the home bar and pause) → swipe Chrome up to close it → relaunch and revisit the site
④ If still blocked, uninstall and reinstall Chrome (last resort)
gps.help_android_body:
① Chrome site permission: tap the lock icon at the left of the address bar → Permissions → Location → Allow
② OS Location: Settings → Location → On → recommend Improve accuracy mode
③ Chrome app permission: Settings → Apps → Chrome → Permissions → Location → Allow only while using the app
gps.help_desktop_body:
① Browser site permission: click the lock icon at the left of the address bar → Location → Allow
② macOS: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Location Services → enable your browser
③ Windows: Settings → Privacy → Location → enable Let apps access your location → enable Let desktop apps access your location
gps.help_https_note: ※ Geolocation is always blocked over http://. Always access the site via https://ori.pics or https://www.ori.pics.

why.title: We follow open international standards, not a walled garden
why.body:
Every proof image with a public link automatically carries a C2PA standard manifest.
Even if our site disappears, provenance is independently verifiable in any C2PA-aware tool.
why.point_c2pa: The content provenance and authenticity standard built by Adobe, Microsoft, Sony, BBC, and Intel — auto-attached to every proof image published with a public link.
why.point_jpeg_trust: ISO/IEC 21617 (JPEG Trust) compatible. Verification responds in the Trust Report shape with an overall trust level.
why.point_open: No vendor lock-in — verifiable on contentcredentials.org, Adobe Photoshop, Verify by Truepic, and any other C2PA-aware tool.

items.a: We support most common image formats including PNG, JPG (JPEG), WebP, BMP, TIFF, and GIF. Selected images are automatically converted to PNG for certification processing. Maximum file size is 50MB.

items.q: How does the original certification work?
items.a: OriPics uses steganography technology to invisibly embed certification data into the pixel data of your image. When a certified image is selected again, the embedded data is extracted to instantly verify its authenticity. Even a single pixel modification is detected.

items.q: Can I share a certified image with others?
items.a: Yes! By creating a Quick Link, anyone can verify the original certification status in their web browser. Quick Links remain valid for 7 days on the Free plan, and for as long as you subscribe with Pro's Storage Box. Note: Sending the image file directly through social media (KakaoTalk, Instagram, WhatsApp, etc.) may break the certification, as these platforms automatically compress and resize images. To preserve the certification, we recommend sharing via Quick Link. When you share a public link in a messenger (KakaoTalk, LINE, Slack, iMessage, etc.), a small photo thumbnail appears in the chat; that thumbnail is briefly cached by the messenger service and does not affect the certified original.

items.q: Are my images stored on the server?
items.a: Your images are not stored on the server. Certification is processed directly on your device (browser). Only when you publish a Quick Link is the certified result image stored in secure cloud storage — for 7 days on the Free plan, or for as long as you subscribe with Pro's Storage Box. Verification also never sends your image to the server.

No. OriPics converts to lossless PNG format for certification, so there is absolutely no quality degradation. Only imperceptible data is embedded — indistinguishable from the original to the human eye.

items.q: What happens when I select an animated image (GIF, WebP, APNG, etc.)?
items.a: Animated images such as GIF, animated WebP, and APNG contain multiple frames, but OriPics certifies only the first frame. The certified result is saved as a static PNG image. Animation is not preserved.

items.q: Is GPS location included when I take a photo?
items.a: Yes. When you shoot in the OriPics mobile app with location access allowed, the GPS coordinates at the moment of capture are embedded into the image pixels under the server signature. If you create a Quick Link, the capture location is also shown on the viewer page. You can turn GPS off anytime on the camera screen. File selection and other non-camera methods do not include GPS to prevent tampering.

items.q: Does editing EXIF metadata (timestamp, GPS) with an EXIF editor affect OriPics certification?
items.a: No, it has zero effect. The timestamp, GPS, and resolution that OriPics certifies are embedded directly into the image pixels via steganography — not stored in EXIF. EXIF is just plain text metadata that anyone can freely edit or delete, but OriPics verification ignores EXIF entirely and extracts only the original information encoded in the pixels. So no matter how you alter the EXIF values, the verified timestamp and GPS will always show the original values recorded at the moment of certification. And if even a single pixel is modified, it is instantly detected as tampering. Note that the C2PA Content Credentials attached to published images are signed over the file including its metadata — so editing and re-saving EXIF may break C2PA validation or strip the credentials. This is C2PA working as designed, leaving evidence of tampering. Even then, as long as the pixels are unchanged, OriPics verification can still confirm the image is original (dual protection).

items.q: Are high-resolution images certified at original size?
items.a: Yes. For images whose longest side exceeds 1800 pixels, you can choose to certify a standard size (proportionally resized to 1800 pixels), the original size, or both. Original-size certification uses more credits depending on size (2× the standard rate, 3× above 100 megapixels). Images at 1800 pixels or smaller are certified as-is.

items.q: What's the difference between Standard and Verified certification?
items.a: Both tiers provide the same integrity guarantee from the moment of certification onward — the server signs the image's pixel data at certification time, so changing even a single pixel afterward is detected. The difference is how much you can trust what happened before certification. Standard seals any image (e.g., from your gallery), proving it has remained unmodified since that moment. Verified is granted only to photos taken with the OriPics mobile app camera (Pro plan): through iOS App Attest / Android Play Integrity hardware attestation, Apple/Google confirm that a genuine app on a real device requested certification at the moment of capture. Both tiers are clearly distinguished on verification results and public link pages.

items.q: How can I sign up or log in?
items.a: OriPics supports Apple, Google, Kakao, and Naver social login as well as email/password sign-up, on both web and the mobile app. With social login, an account is created automatically with a single tap. Signing in with the same social account connects you to the same OriPics account on both web and app.

items.q: I see "This email is already registered with another method."
items.a: An OriPics account is unique per email address. For example, if you first signed up with Kakao and later try Google login with the same email, we don't link them automatically for security reasons — instead we guide you to sign in with your original method (the message shows the email and the method). Note that the email used by each social login is the one registered with that service, so if the emails differ across services, separate accounts will be created.

items.q: What happens if I choose 'Hide My Email' with Apple login?
items.a: You'll be signed up under an Apple relay address (@privaterelay.appleid.com), so it won't match accounts created with your real email via other methods. To use one account across web and app, we recommend choosing 'Share My Email' on your first Apple login. Apple remembers this choice for future logins; to change it, remove the OriPics connection in your Apple account settings (Sign-In & Security → Sign in with Apple) and log in again.

items.q: What happens to social login connections when I delete my account?
items.a: Deleting your account removes your OriPics data and also disconnects the social login link — OriPics disappears from the 'connected services' list of each provider. If you sign in with the same social account again later, you'll go through the consent screen as a first-time user and a brand-new account will be created; data from before deletion (proofs, links, remaining credits) cannot be restored.

items.q: Can I certify a large batch of photos at once?
items.a: The web and app are designed for certifying photos individually or in small batches. If you need to certify hundreds of photos at once (asset audits, bulk field records, archive provenance, etc.), we support batch processing and API integration — email hi@ori.pics with your volume and use case and we'll suggest an approach and pricing.

items.q: What happens when I use up my Pro certifications? Do leftovers carry over?
items.a: Open Subscription in your profile and tap 'Renew now'. The card you registered when subscribing is charged one month (₩9,900) immediately, your certifications reset to the plan amount, and your next billing date restarts from that day. No payment window opens. When your remaining count drops to 10% of the plan or less, a banner appears in your profile so you can renew before heading to a site. Remaining certifications do not carry over; they expire when you renew, and the confirmation dialog shows how many will expire. If you only need 10 more app captures urgently, a One-Day Pass (coming soon) is an option. Renewal payments follow the same refund rules in Article 11 of the Terms.

items.q: How do I join the Partner Relay Challenge?
items.a: Every member automatically gets a numeric partner code. Enter a friend's code on the sign-up form (or within 7 days of signing up, in Profile or the app's Settings) and you both receive a 50% Pro coupon (₩4,950). When 12 people sign up with your code and complete their first proof, you get six 1-month Pro free vouchers (applied automatically to 6 consecutive charges after your coupons are used up). Coupons apply automatically to each Pro monthly charge (up to 2 on the first charge) and are valid for 24 months. Partner status (earning on referrals) is limited to the first 500 members, and accrual ends December 31, 2026. See the Partner page for details.

faq.q: Where do I find my partner code?
faq.a: It's assigned automatically at sign-up. On the web: Profile > Partner Relay Challenge; in the app: Settings tab > Partner. You can copy and share it there.

faq.q: I signed up with Google/Apple/Kakao/Naver. Where do I enter a code?
faq.a: In the prompt right after your first login, in the Profile partner card, or in the app's Settings tab — once, within 7 days of signing up.

faq.q: I'm already a member. Can I join?
faq.a: Yes. Members who signed up before the challenge was announced can enter a code once at any time during the challenge.

No redemption needed — they apply automatically to Pro monthly charges. Up to 2 on the first charge (₩0), then 1 per charge (₩{amount}); once coupons run out, 1-month free vouchers are used one per consecutive charge. Valid for {months24} months from issuance.

faq.q: What happens after the first 500 partners are filled?
faq.a: You still get your own coupon when you sign up with a code. Only partners (within the 500) earn coupons when others use their code and qualify for the {goal}-friend bonus. Partners keep earning after the cap is filled, until the challenge ends.

A friend counts as a 'valid referral' once they complete their first photo proof. At {goal}, {months} one-month free vouchers are issued within 24 hours after review and you're notified by email. They apply one per charge for {months} consecutive months after your coupons are used up.

notice: Period: benefits are granted for sign-ups and joins until the challenge end date. Partner status (earning on referrals) is limited to the first {cap} members by join order; closure is shown on this page.

Coupons (₩{amount}) and 1-month free vouchers apply automatically to Pro monthly charges only (vouchers are used one per consecutive charge) — not to Day Passes, annual billing, or Business plans. Valid {months24} months from issuance; no cash refund, transfer, or resale; not a prepaid payment instrument.
A registered card is still required for a month reduced to ₩0. The 2-coupon first charge applies once per account.
The {goal}-friend bonus ({months} one-month free vouchers) counts 'valid referrals' (first proof completed) and is issued after review. Once per account.
Benefits obtained through fake accounts, self-referral, or other abuse may be revoked and participation voided (benefits already used are not clawed back).
Refunds for charges with a benefit applied follow Terms §7 based on the amount actually paid; coupons are restored for a full refund within 7 days without use.

Code owners' names are partially masked in lookups. Referral relationships are retained for one year after the challenge for benefit issuance and fraud prevention. We may change conditions or end early with prior notice.
